Welcome to the UGREEN NAS Community FAQ Hub 👋




This is a living thread bringing together the questions UGREEN NAS users ask most often across our communities and social platforms—from initial setup and remote access to backups, surveillance, transfer speeds, and hardware behavior.




We’ll update this post weekly as new questions come in and as UGOS Pro continues to evolve.




Note: Menu names and feature availability may vary slightly depending on your NAS model, UGOS Pro version, and app version.

1. Setup & Remote Access


1.1 How can I access my NAS when I’m away from home?

For most users, UGREENlink is the easiest option:

Go to Control Panel > Device Connection > Remote Access.

Enable UGREENlink Remote Access Service.

Sign in to your UGREEN Cloud account.

Create a UGREENlink ID.

Connect through the UGREEN NAS mobile app, desktop client, or the generated browser link.

Before enabling remote access, use a strong, unique password and enable two-factor authentication (2FA).

Advanced users can also consider DDNS or Tailscale, depending on their network and security requirements. See the official remote access guide for a full comparison.




1.2 Why can a user still not write to a shared folder after being granted Read/Write access?

In UGOS Pro, a user’s effective access may be affected by both direct user permissions and inherited User Group permissions. 

When permissions conflict, the current priority is: 

Access Denied > Read Only > Read/Write > Not set

This means a restrictive User Group permission can override a more permissive setting assigned directly to the user. 

If the result is not what you expected, open the user’s Permissions & Settings page and check: 

Permissions assigned directly to the user 

Permissions inherited from every User Group they belong to 

Whether the restriction applies to the top-level Shared Folder or a subfolder 

For data that requires genuinely different access boundaries, separate top-level Shared Folders are generally easier to audit than multiple exceptions nested under one folder.




1.3 For external collaboration, when should you use a restricted user account, a sharing link or a file-collection link?

Choose the access method based on how long the access should last and whether the recipient needs to read, write or only upload data. 

Restricted Standard User account: best for recurring access to selected Shared Folders. The account remains subject to its assigned user and User Group permissions. 

UGREENlink sharing link: better for temporary viewing or downloading. The link can be protected with an expiration date, password and access-count limit. 

File-collection link: use Request files when someone only needs to upload data to a selected destination without receiving continuing access to the NAS. 

A sharing link should not replace a managed user account when ongoing read/write access is required. Conversely, creating a persistent NAS account for a one-time download or upload gives the recipient more continuing access than the task requires. 

The practical rule is: 

Recurring collaboration → restricted account

Temporary download → sharing link

Temporary upload → file-collection link







1.4 How can I tell whether a remote connection problem comes from the NAS, VPN, SMB or client device?

Test one layer at a time instead of reinstalling every application. 

Confirm that the same client can reach the NAS on the local network.

From the remote network, test whether the NAS web interface or UGREENlink is reachable.

If using a VPN, verify that the NAS is reachable through the VPN tunnel, and test its LAN IP address or hostname rather than assuming it has a separate "VPN IP."

Test browser access before mounting the SMB share.

Try the same remote connection from a second client device.

Use the results to narrow down the cause: 

Browser works but SMB fails: check the saved mount address, credentials, SMB settings and VPN route. Note that browser access only proves IP reachability, not SMB reachability, since they use different ports and protocols.

Other devices work but one client fails: focus on that client's firewall, permissions, cached credentials and network settings.

Neither browser nor SMB works remotely: check VPN connectivity and routing before changing NAS file-sharing settings.

Local access also fails: investigate the NAS service or local network first.

Keep in mind that a VPN does not automatically break SMB, but it can change the network path, source IP or routing in ways that invalidate an existing SMB session. This makes SMB failures more likely over VPN. 

Do not expose SMB directly to the public Internet as a troubleshooting shortcut.




2. System Updates & Troubleshooting




2.1 How should I prepare for a UGOS Pro update, and what should I do if it fails?

Before updating:

Read the release notes and check for any model-specific notices.

Back up important data and make sure the backup can be opened.

If you are updating manually, download the firmware only from the official UGREEN Download Center and select your exact NAS model.

Use stable power, pause important transfers and other heavy tasks, and do not turn off the NAS or remove any drives while the update is running.

If you use SSD Cache on a system version earlier than 1.17.0.0095, it is strongly recommended that you remove the cache in Storage Manager before updating and recreate it afterward.

If the update fails, record your NAS model, current and target versions, error message, time of failure, screenshots, and any available logs. Do not repeatedly reset the NAS, reinstall the system, or remove drives unless UGREEN Support instructs you to do so. Submit a technical support ticket for the next steps.




2.2 What should I do if my NAS freezes or restarts unexpectedly?

First determine what failed: 

App failure: Only one application is unavailable. 

Network failure: The NAS is running, but the web interface and shared folders cannot be reached. 

System freeze: UGOS Pro, SSH, file services and apps all stop responding while the LEDs remain on. 

Unexpected restart: The NAS reboots without a normal shutdown. 

After access is restored: 

Record the exact incident time and time zone. 

Export the system and application logs immediately. 

Note the active workload, such as transcoding, Docker, VM, backup or a large SMB transfer. 

Record recent firmware, RAM, drive, network or peripheral changes. 

Check the power source, UPS events, temperatures and storage-pool status. 




For media-related freezes, also record whether playback used Direct Play or transcoding, whether hardware acceleration was enabled, and the codec, subtitles and client involved. 

Temporarily stop the suspected workload and test one change at a time. Do not repeatedly force the NAS off or apply unofficial system modifications. 

If the issue repeats, submit a support ticket with the logs, timestamp and reproduction steps. A precise timeline is more useful than a general description such as "the NAS crashed."




2.3 What should I do if my NAS remains stuck on "Shutting down"?

A long shutdown can be caused by unfinished writes, application or container stop timeouts, indexing, database cleanup, or storage maintenance. Do not assume that a blinking power light means it is safe to disconnect the NAS. 

Before forcing power off: 

Stop accessing the NAS from other devices.

If the interface is still available, check for active transfers, RAID operations, Data Organizing, backups and container tasks.

Record when shutdown was started and whether the HDD and network LEDs are still active.

Do not remove drives, disconnect the UPS or repeatedly press the power button.

If the NAS remains inaccessible, record the model, UGOS Pro version, LED state and elapsed time before contacting Support.

There is no universal timeout after which forced shutdown becomes risk-free. If storage maintenance or active writes may still be running, disconnecting power can leave the storage pool inconsistent. 

After any forced power loss, check the storage-pool status, system logs and drive health before restarting heavy transfers or maintenance tasks.




2.4 How can I tell whether "read-only" is caused by folder permissions or the storage pool?

"Read-only" can describe two different problems. Identify the affected layer before changing permissions. 

Try creating a test folder in File Manager using an administrator account.

Test another shared folder on the same volume.

Check the storage pool, volume and drive status for warnings or degradation.

Confirm whether the problem affects every user and application, or only one SMB user or container.

Use the result to narrow it down: 

- One user, share or container is affected: Check the account permissions, shared-folder ACL and container mount path. 

- Every share on the volume is read-only: Stop non-essential workloads and check the pool, volume, drive health and system logs. 

- Files work in File Manager but not in a container: Verify the bind mount and the container's user/group permissions. 

Do not immediately apply recursive chmod or chown commands. They can overwrite existing ACLs across an entire folder tree. Record the affected path, account, storage status and recent system changes before contacting Support.




3. Storage & Data Protection


3.1 Can I hide specific photos or videos from the Photos app?

There is currently no dedicated Hidden category in the Photos app.

For sensitive files, you can store them in Vault app. If you only need basic access control, another option is to keep the files in your Personal Folder and manage the folder permissions carefully.

We’ve also passed the request for a simpler hide function to the product team for evaluation.



3.2 Why isn’t photo backup running in the background on my iPhone?

Please check the following:

Background App Refresh is enabled for the UGREEN NAS app.

Low Power Mode is turned off.

The app has permission to access your photos.

The app has not been force-closed from the app switcher.

If the issue continues, upload the mobile app logs through:

Avatar > About > Log Upload

When contacting support, include the approximate time when the issue occurred so the team can locate the relevant logs more quickly.



3.3 Which photo and cloud sources can currently sync or back up to UGREEN NAS?

Phone gallery: Supported, including automatic photo backup. Background behavior is subject to mobile operating system restrictions.

Google Drive: Supported.

Google Photos: Direct import or synchronization is not currently supported.

iCloud: Direct transfer from iCloud is not currently supported. Download the files to your iPhone or iPad first, then use the UGREEN NAS app to back them up to your NAS. 




3.4 Can I change RAID type or expand my storage pool without deleting data?

UGREEN NAS supports changing the RAID mode of a storage pool without losing existing data. The supported upgrade path is Basic → RAID 1 → RAID 5. Note that upgrading from Basic to RAID 5 requires first converting to RAID 1 as an intermediate step. The storage pool must be in a healthy state, and every new drive added must be at least as large as the smallest existing drive in the pool. JBOD and RAID 0 configurations cannot be converted. For capacity expansion by replacing drives, swap one drive at a time and allow each rebuild to complete before replacing the next.




3.5 What is the best way to back up or sync data to USB, another NAS, or cloud storage?

Use Sync & Backup and choose the task type that matches the goal: sync for keeping locations aligned, backup for recoverable copies, and an external-drive task for USB storage. Keep the backup destination separate from the source, schedule the task, enable versioning where available, and run a small restore test. For important data, follow the 3-2-1 rule: three copies, two storage types, and one copy off-site.




3.6 How can I check whether my NAS backup really works?

A backup task showing “Successful” confirms that the job completed, but it does not always guarantee that every file can be recovered correctly. 

A simple restore test can help you check the full process. 

Choose a small test set

Select a few different types of non-sensitive files, such as: a document, a photo, a video and a folder containing several files.

Include at least one file that is important enough to represent your real backup needs.

Restore to a separate location

Restore the test files to a temporary folder rather than overwriting the originals.

This lets you compare both versions safely and avoids accidental data loss during the test.

Open and inspect the restored files

Do not stop after checking that the filenames appear.

Confirm that:

• Documents open normally

• Photos and videos are not corrupted

• Folder structures remain intact

• File sizes look correct

• Important dates and metadata are preserved where required

Record the result

Note when the test was completed, which files were restored and whether any problems occurred.

Repeat the test periodically and after major changes to your storage or backup configuration.

Remember

RAID, snapshots, synchronization and backup protect against different risks.

RAID helps maintain availability after certain drive failures.

Snapshots can help recover earlier file versions.

Sync keeps files consistent between locations. 

A separate backup protects you when the original data is deleted, corrupted or otherwise unavailable. 

For important data, consider using a 3-2-1 strategy and test at least one of those copies before you need it.




3.7 Should I use an NVMe SSD for cache or create an SSD storage pool?

Choose based on the workload.

Use SSD Cache when:

Your main data is stored on an HDD pool.

The same small files are accessed repeatedly.

Indexing, thumbnails, or multiple users create frequent random reads and writes.

SSD Cache accelerates an existing storage pool. It is not a separate place where you directly store and organize files.

Use an SSD storage pool when:

You want a separate high-speed workspace.

You run apps, containers, databases, or virtual machines.

Active projects need consistently low latency.

An SSD storage pool should be backed up like any other primary storage.

SSD Cache may provide little benefit for one-time transfers of large sequential files, especially when the real bottleneck is the network or another device.

Before buying an SSD, confirm that your NAS supports the intended cache or storage-pool setup and check the exact SSD model in UGREEN’s compatibility list. M.2 SSD hot swapping is not supported. Power off the NAS before physically installing or removing an M.2 SSD, and follow the installation instructions for your model. If the SSD is being used as cache, remove or disable the cache in the UGOS Pro management interface before physically removing the drive.




3.8 Can a Rapid SMART test return Normal while a drive warning still requires investigation?

Yes. A Normal Rapid SMART result is one data point, not a complete clearance of the drive or storage pool.
Interpret it together with:

The current storage-pool state


System notifications and previous test records


Whether the drive has disappeared or reconnected


Changes in reallocated, pending or uncorrectable sectors


CRC errors or other connection-related events


New noise, temperature changes or failed I/O

The distinction between the counters also matters. Increasing reallocated, pending or uncorrectable sectors can indicate media problems, while CRC errors may point to the connection path or backplane rather than the disk surface itself.
A change from the drive’s own previous baseline is often more useful than applying one raw-value threshold to every drive model.
If a warning persists or the relevant counts continue rising, confirm the independent backup and investigate before returning the NAS to a heavy workload.



3.9 What does UGOS Pro Data Organizing verify and what does it not verify?

Data Organizing is available for eligible RAID 5 and RAID 6 storage pools whose status is Normal or Warning.
It checks consistency across the array and can expose unreadable areas or cases where the stored data and parity do not agree.
However, Data Organizing is not:


A SMART test of an individual drive


A RAID rebuild or drive-replacement process


A backup or restore test


A way to recover deleted or overwritten files


A guarantee against every form of silent corruption

Do not run it during a RAID rebuild, drive replacement, pool expansion, Full SMART test or major backup operation.
The practical distinction is:
SMART tests evaluate individual drives.
Data Organizing checks RAID 5/6 array consistency.
A restore test confirms whether your backup can actually be recovered.
These checks complement one another; none of them replaces the others.




3.10 Can I switch an existing EXT4 volume to Btrfs without recreating it?

UGOS Pro does not support changing an existing volume's filesystem in place. To switch from EXT4 to Btrfs, back up your data, recreate the volume with Btrfs, and restore your files. 

Recreating the volume erases its contents, so verify that your backup can be restored before proceeding. 

If you need snapshots, choose Btrfs when creating the volume. EXT4 volumes do not support UGOS Pro snapshots.

Further reading: Filesystem selection and volume setup




3.11 Why are older snapshots still there after I shorten the retention period? Does locking make them immutable?

Locked snapshots are excluded from automatic retention cleanup, so they can remain even after you shorten the retention period. Administrators can still delete them manually: locking prevents automatic cleanup, not administrator deletion. 

When reviewing snapshot storage usage, check both the retention settings and the lock status of existing snapshots. Changes to or deletion of protected files can increase the space used by snapshots.

Before deleting a snapshot, confirm that you no longer need it as a recovery point. If storage usage remains unexplained after these checks, contact our support team for further investigation.

Further reading: Snapshot retention and recovery protection




3.12 Can I replace my current RAID drives with larger ones one at a time? When will the extra capacity become available?

Replacing drives with larger-capacity models does not necessarily increase your usable storage immediately. 

In most RAID configurations, capacity remains limited by the smallest drives in the array. If your RAID type and storage system support expansion through drive replacement, replace only one drive at a time and wait for the RAID rebuild to complete before replacing the next one. 

Before starting: 

Confirm that your RAID type supports this expansion method. 

Make sure your important data has a separate backup. 

Check that the current storage pool and all drives are healthy. 

Confirm that the replacement drives are compatible and at least as large as the existing drives. 

Do not restart, remove another drive, or interrupt the rebuild unless instructed. 

After the required drives have been replaced and rebuilt, you may still need to expand the storage pool or volume in the storage manager. The exact process depends on the RAID configuration and current UGOS Pro version.




3.13 Why is an external drive detected by the NAS but unavailable to Files, Sync & Backup or SMB?

Check where access stops:

Not shown in Storage Manager: Test the cable, port, enclosure and power supply.

Detected but not mounted in Files: Check the filesystem. UGOS Pro supports FAT16/FAT32, exFAT, NTFS, Btrfs, ext2/3/4 and XFS; HFS+ and APFS are unsupported.

Accessible in Files but unavailable to Sync & Backup: Confirm that the selected destination is writable, has sufficient space and still points to the correct mount path after reconnection.


Accessible locally but not over SMB: Check whether the drive is exposed through the file service and whether the connecting account has permission.


Repeatedly disconnects: Connect it directly, then test another cable or port and verify that the enclosure has sufficient power.

Do not format or initialize the drive until any existing data has been copied to another verified location.




4. Media & Theater




4.1 Can I change the video skip or rewind interval to five seconds?

Not currently. The skip-forward and rewind intervals are fixed at 15 seconds and cannot be customized at this time.




4.2 Should I use Plex, Jellyfin, or the built-in Theater app?

Choose Theater for the simplest built-in experience, Jellyfin for a free and privacy-focused media server, and Plex for a polished client ecosystem and easier remote use. Install Plex/Jellyfin from App Center when your model offers it; otherwise use Docker only on models that support Docker. Give the app read access to your media folders and keep its configuration/database on persistent storage. Hardware-transcoding support depends on the model, app, and codec. Also note that Plex hardware transcoding requires a Plex Pass subscription. 




4.3 Why is Theater grouping or identifying my movies and TV shows incorrectly? 

Incorrect grouping or identification usually happens when the filename does not match what the media scraper expects. The scraper pulls metadata from TMDB based on the filename — it looks for the title and year first, and extra information like resolution or release group can interfere with matching. 

Recommended naming conventions: 

Movies: Title (Year) — e.g. Fast Charlie (2023) 

TV series: Series.Title.Year.SXXEYY — e.g. A Certain Scientific Railgun.2010.S01E01 

Extras/Specials: use S00EXX — e.g. A Certain Scientific Railgun.2010.S00E01.mkv 

Additional tips: 

Keep movies and TV shows in separate root folders.
Avoid extra info like resolution or release group unless you're sure the scraper can handle it.
If the scraper still picks the wrong match, you can manually correct it inside Theater by searching and assigning the correct title.




4.4 Why does the same video play smoothly on one device but buffer on another?

The file may be the same, but the two playback devices may not support it in the same way. 

A media server generally uses one of three playback methods: 

Direct Play sends the original file to the client without converting it. This places very little additional load on the NAS. 

Direct Stream keeps the original video but may change the container or convert the audio. 

Transcoding converts the video into a format, resolution or bitrate that the client can handle. This requires significantly more processing power. 

A file may Direct Play on a TV but transcode in a browser or mobile app. This usually comes down to differences in: 

Video or audio codec support 

File-container compatibility 

Subtitle format 

Display resolution 

HDR support 

Available network bandwidth 

Playback-quality settings 

Subtitles are an easy detail to overlook. Some subtitle formats—especially image-based ones like PGS—must be burned into the video, turning what could have been a simple Direct Play session into a full transcode. 

When playback buffers, check the media server's dashboard or playback information first. Look for whether the session is using Direct Play, Direct Stream or Transcode, then check the reason shown for the conversion. 

If the file Direct Plays locally but buffers remotely, the limiting factor may be the home internet upload speed or the remote client's quality setting rather than the NAS itself.



5. Apps & Containers




5.1 How do I get started with Docker or Docker Compose on UGREEN NAS?

Docker availability depends on your NAS model — if you don't see it in App Center, your model does not support it. Use the GUI for a single container and Compose when several services need shared networks, folders, or environment variables. Before starting, create dedicated folders, map persistent configuration/data paths, give the container only the permissions it needs, and make sure host ports do not conflict.




5.2 Why does the same Docker Compose stack work in UGOS Pro Docker but fail when deployed through Portainer?

Even when the Compose file looks identical, the deployment environment may be different. 

Check the following:

Environment variables: Make sure the same .env values are available. 

Relative paths: Portainer may resolve relative paths from a different working directory. Use absolute paths where possible. 

Folder permissions: Confirm that the container user has access to every bind-mounted folder. 

Ports: Check whether another container or UGOS Pro service is already using the required port. 

Networks: Confirm that the expected Docker networks exist and that service names can resolve correctly. 

Generated configuration: Compare the fully resolved Compose configuration rather than only the original YAML file. 

Logs and health checks: A container marked as “running” may still be unable to reach its database or other services. 

If one deployment works and the other does not, compare paths, permissions, environment variables and networks before changing the application itself.




5.3 How can I update a Docker container without losing data or making rollback difficult?

Treat the container image as replaceable and its persistent data as something that must be protected separately. 

Before updating: confirm mounts and back up key configuration

Confirm the mount paths: Open the Docker app, go to the container's settings, and check the "Storage" or "Volumes" mapping. Make sure critical paths such as /config and /data are mapped to real folders on the NAS (for example, /volume1/docker/jellyfin/config).

Back up the Compose file or run parameters: If you deployed with Docker Compose, simply back up the docker-compose.yml file. If you used docker run manually, record the image tag, port mappings, environment variables, and other key parameters.

Perform the update: pull the new image and recreate the container

Pull the new image: In the Docker app's "Images" page, find the image and click "Pull" or "Update." If you want to pin a version for easier rollback, specify a tag when pulling (for example, jellyfin:10.8.13) instead of using latest. You can also enable auto-update in the settings of the Docker to reduce manual efforts.

Stop and recreate the container: Stop the old container, then create a new one using the new image. Key point: when recreating, you must use exactly the same port mappings, environment variables, and volume mounts as the old container.

Rollback plan: what if something goes wrong?

If the new container fails to start or behaves abnormally, rollback is simple because your data is still there:

Just delete the malfunctioning new container, then recreate a container using the old image tag (for example, jellyfin:10.8.12) and mount the same NAS data folder. Your service will return to its pre-update state.

Does deleting the container delete the data?

Deleting a container does not mean deleting your data. As long as the data was mounted to a local NAS folder from the start, you can delete the container and recreate it from the old image, and your data will still be intact. What actually gets lost is data that was never mounted out and only existed inside the container.




6. Power Management




6.1 Can I schedule Energy Saving mode during specific hours?

You can manually enable Energy Saving mode under:

Control Panel > Hardware & Power > General > Power Management




At present, UGOS Pro does not support scheduling Energy Saving mode for specific time periods. The setting must be changed manually.

The request for scheduled switching has been shared with the product team for further consideration.




6.2 Do I need a UPS, and how should I set up automatic shutdown?

A UPS is strongly recommended if your location experiences power outages, voltage drops, or unstable power.

Before buying one:

Check the exact UPS model in UGREEN’s compatibility list.

Make sure its output wattage can support the NAS and any other essential devices.

Choose enough battery runtime for the NAS to complete a safe shutdown.

Confirm that the UPS can communicate with UGOS Pro through a supported USB or network connection.

Connect the NAS to a battery-backed outlet. If your setup relies on network signaling, or you want network access during the outage, connect the required router or switch to battery-backed power as well.

In UGOS Pro, go to Control Panel > Hardware & Power > UPS. Confirm that the UPS is detected, then enable automatic shutdown and choose a sensible delay.

Test the setup while the NAS is idle by briefly disconnecting mains power according to the UPS manufacturer’s instructions. Confirm that UGOS Pro detects battery operation and begins the expected shutdown process.

The UPS manufacturer’s advertised runtime is for reference only. Actual runtime depends on battery condition, connected load, and device activity.




6.3 Why do my HDDs keep waking up when no one is using the NAS?

Have you ever noticed your NAS drives spinning up even when no one seems to be using it? A NAS can look idle from the outside while background services are still accessing its drives. 

Common sources of disk activity include: 

Media-library scans 

Photo indexing and thumbnail generation 

Containers or applications writing logs or databases 

Scheduled tasks 

SMART checks and storage maintenance 

Computers reconnecting to shared folders 

Monitoring tools polling drive information 

System or application updates 

Even a very small read or write can wake a drive from standby. 

Start by noting when the drives wake up. If it happens at roughly the same time each day, review scheduled tasks and maintenance jobs. If it happens repeatedly throughout the day, check active applications, containers, connected clients and system logs. 

Temporarily pausing one non-essential service at a time can help identify the source. Avoid disabling multiple services at once, since that makes it harder to determine which one was responsible. 

HDD standby should not be treated as a requirement for every setup, either. A NAS running media services, containers, surveillance recording or frequent indexing may legitimately keep its drives active. Repeatedly waking and sleeping the disks may also introduce delays whenever a service needs them again. 

If the activity is accompanied by SMART warnings, repeated clicking, unusually high temperatures or a degraded storage pool, back up important data and investigate the drive health separately.




6.4 Why does Docker storage keep growing even when my application data is saved in a shared folder?

A bind mount may protect your main application data, but it does not automatically move every file created by the container. 

Storage can still be consumed by: 

- Container logs without rotation 

- Image layers and unused images 

- Temporary or cache files 

- Databases written to an unmapped internal path 

- Old containers and volumes left after updates 

Before deleting anything: 

Identify whether the space is used by images, logs, volumes or application data.

Confirm that every persistent path required by the application is mapped to the intended NAS folder.

Set log-size and rotation limits where supported.

Export or back up databases and configuration files.

Remove only resources confirmed as unused.

Do not delete the Docker data directory or an unknown volume to recover space quickly. A container can often be recreated, but data stored only inside its internal volume can't be recoverable once deleted.



7. Surveillance Center


7.1 Which cameras are compatible with Surveillance Center?

Surveillance Center supports IP cameras that use the standard ONVIF or RTSP protocols, making it compatible with many mainstream network cameras.

Compatibility may still depend on the camera’s firmware, authentication method, and video stream settings. Before adding a camera, make sure ONVIF or RTSP is enabled and that the correct IP address, port, username, and password are being used.



7.2 Why does Surveillance Center say that H.265 is not supported?

This warning commonly appears when Surveillance Center is being accessed through a web browser. H.265 is subject to licensing requirements, so many web browsers do not support it natively.

For the most consistent playback experience, use the latest UGREEN NAS desktop client instead of browser playback.

You can download the Windows or macOS client from the official download page.

If H.265 playback also fails in the desktop client, check the camera’s stream format and codec profile, then contact support with the camera model and relevant logs.




7.3 Why can I see a camera's live view but Surveillance Center cannot record it?

Open the camera's Settings > Storage Settings. You will see three recording options: 24/7 Recording, Events only, and Do not record. Make sure the current option is not set to "Do not record".

If "Events only" is selected

Recording is triggered only when the AI detects a qualifying event. If the recording window is short and no triggerable event occurs during that period — such as a detected face, package, or pet — no video will be recorded. This is expected behavior, not a fault.

If "24/7 Recording" is selected but no video is recorded

That is genuinely abnormal. Collect the logs and contact UGREEN technical support for further analysis.



8. Network & Hardware


8.1 Why am I only getting around 8–10 MB/s when my NAS has a much faster Ethernet port?

A fast NAS port does not guarantee the same end-to-end transfer speed. Every device between the NAS and your computer must support the intended network speed.

Check the following possible causes:

UGREENlink remote access

The UGREENlink free service supports speeds of approximately 8 MB/s per device. For higher remote transfer speeds, you can use a third-party DDNS service.

Local network bottlenecks

Your router, switch, hub, network adapter, or other network equipment may be limiting the connection speed.

Go to Control Panel > Network > Network Connections and check the current link speed. If it shows 100 Mbps, this is likely the bottleneck.

SMB encryption or signing may also place a heavy load on the client device’s CPU and limit transfer performance.


Transferring large numbers of small files

Small-file transfers are normally slower because the system must perform frequent I/O operations for file indexing and metadata processing.


When asking the community for help, please include your NAS model, link speed, connection method, client device, and whether the test was local or remote.



8.2 Why does the iDX6011 PSU fan repeatedly start and stop?

The PSU fan is controlled by the power supply’s internal temperature and load. It starts when the load increases and the internal temperature rises above the preset threshold, and stops when the load and temperature fall below the stop threshold.

The PSU fan operates independently of the system and chassis fans and cannot be adjusted through firmware or system fan settings.

This start-and-stop behavior is normal and depends on the current workload. It does not affect normal device operation. If you are unsure whether the sound you are hearing is normal airflow noise, please contact technical support for further assistance.




8.3 Is this NAS noise or temperature normal, and how can I reduce it?

Some noise is normal. You may hear steady fan airflow, occasional HDD seek sounds, or louder activity while the NAS is indexing files, backing up data, or rebuilding a RAID array.

Buzzing or rattling can also come from drive-tray or surface vibration rather than a failing drive.

Try these checks:

Review the current workload, drive health, SMART status, and temperatures in UGOS Pro.

Place the NAS on a solid, stable surface.

Keep the air vents clear, with approximately 10 cm of space behind the NAS and 5 cm on each side.

Power off and unplug the NAS before cleaning dust from its vents.

Temporarily select a higher fan speed to see whether temperatures improve.

Repeated clicking, grinding, or loud clunking, SMART warnings, missing airflow, or temperatures that continue to rise are warning signs. Back up important data, stop non-essential workloads, and contact UGREEN Support.

Before replacing a fan or modifying the chassis, check with Support. Unauthorized modifications, or damage caused by disassembly, may affect warranty coverage.

Contact us by email or submit a service ticket:

nas-support@ugreen.com

Submit a technical support ticket




8.4 Can I connect the two NAS Ethernet ports to different networks?

Yes. On supported multi-port models, each Ethernet port can be assigned an address on a different subnet. 

This is useful for: 

Separating normal access from backup or media traffic 

Connecting a workstation through a dedicated high-speed link 

Allowing controlled access from two routed networks 

When configuring the ports: 

Assign each port an IP address that matches its subnet.

Use only one default gateway unless your network design specifically requires otherwise.

Confirm that routing and firewall rules allow clients to reach the required NAS services.

Test each NAS address separately.

Do not connect two independent ports to the same subnet, as this can create ambiguous network paths. If both ports should work as one connection, use a supported link-aggregation configuration and a compatible switch.

A second NAS port does not automatically combine two Internet connections, provide Internet failover or reduce Wi-Fi congestion. Those functions should normally be managed by the router or firewall. 

For local Jellyfin playback, the TV only needs a reachable local path to the NAS and sufficient LAN bandwidth; it does not require a separate Internet connection.




8.5 Why can a memory module match the required DDR generation and speed but still cause instability?

DDR generation and rated speed alone do not guarantee compatibility. Capacity per module, chip density, rank layout, ECC support, voltage, JEDEC timings and firmware support can also affect whether the NAS boots and remains stable.

Before purchasing: check the exact module part number against the compatibility information for your NAS model here: https://ai.ugreen.com/pages/compatibility
During boot: if you hear 3 long and 2 short beeps, the memory is incompatible with the NAS.


No beep symptom, but still unstable? Boot loops, unexpected restarts or application crashes can still point to a memory problem. Try the following:

Shut down the NAS, then clean the memory slot and the module's gold contacts.

Reinstall the original memory to confirm a stable baseline.

For two-module configurations, use a matched pair with the same capacity and part number.

If instability continues, restore the original memory and contact Tech Support with the NAS model and the complete module part number.
